# Robot Demonstration Data Generation

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](generation_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Robot Demonstration Data Generation

Generate robot demonstration trajectories or training data from real or generated videos, retargeting and simulation optimization. Classify by the main contribution: online retargeting controllers belong under policy/control. Distinguish replay from closed-loop deployment.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.1] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-1"></a> | **DexNinja｜Real2Sim2Real augmentation · Deformable cutting simulation · Visuotactile imitation learning**<br>[DexNinja: Learning Robust Dexterous Cutting Policy with a Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Engine](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17208v1)<br>Haozhe Lou, Runyi Yang, Wanqi Zhong, Caiyun Liu, Yicheng Liu, Wenhao Liu, Wenlong Ma, Jiawei Xia, Kanzhi Wu, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool, Hang Zhao, Yiming Li<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `real-to-sim-to-real` `teleoperation` `demonstration-synthesis` `data-augmentation` `category-conditioned-asset-generation` `physical-randomization` `differentiable-simulation` `deformable-object-manipulation` `food-cutting` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `visuotactile` `imitation-learning` `behavior-cloning` `action-chunking` `stage-conditioned-policy` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | DexNinja reconstructs deformable simulation scenes from limited real-robot cutting demonstrations, varies shapes and physical parameters within food categories, refines and filters cutting trajectories, then combines real and simulated data to train a stage-conditioned visuotactile action-chunking policy for bimanual food stabilization and knife cutting.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Robot teleoperation seeds category-constrained asset generation, quality checks and physical variation; differentiable cutting simulation refines/filters trajectories and records aligned observations/actions. The final ACT-style policy uses supervised behavior cloning: arms handle approach/alignment, hands regulate contact from touch/proprioception. Nominal approach/grasp, knife-positioning and cutting chunks are 64/128/16 steps. The primary platform is DR3/DR5 arms + LinkerHand L10; dual Franka + LinkerBot L20 requires embodiment-specific calibration, kinematics and execution interfaces, not established zero-shot shared-weight transfer. Main-table training uses 5 real + 50 simulated sequences per food (strawberry, apple, banana, potato), with 25 real trials each. Mixed-data success is 50%, versus 31% real-only and 34% sim-only. Generalization mainly covers unseen within-category instances; repeated cutting remains difficult. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17208v1) · [Project](https://dex-ninja.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.2] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-2"></a> | **Human2Dex｜Wrist-view demonstrations · Cross-hand data reuse · Grasp-relative representation**<br>[Human2Dex: Dexterous Robot Learning from Wrist-Centric Human Demonstrations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13119v1)<br>Jiachen Zhang, Yuanyuan Li, Shaqi Luo<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-demonstrations` `wrist-centric-demonstrations` `cross-embodiment` `cross-hand-data-reuse` `demonstration-synthesis` `motion-retargeting` `hand-structure-alignment` `grasp-pocket-interaction-representation` `object-tracking` `diffusion-policy` `imitation-learning` `real-world` | Human2Dex converts shared wrist-centric human demonstrations into hand-specific training data through structural observation alignment and motion retargeting, then conditions separate diffusion policies on GPIR object states relative to the thumb–index grasp center, without collecting task demonstrations on the target robots.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Wrist RGB and PICO tracking capture demonstrations; local hand-appearance randomization and a shared 21-point skeleton align observations, while fused PICO/visual motion is retargeted separately. GPIR supplies object position relative to the thumb–index fingertip midpoint, image area and tracking reliability; auxiliary position/area supervision is removed at deployment. DINOv2 plus Diffusion Policy predicts 16 arm–hand steps, executes eight, then observes again. The same 1,899 human episodes support Linker O6 (6 active DoFs) and Wuji (20 active DoFs). Both perform sponge/croissant pick-and-place, cup insertion, bottle reorientation, egg-carton opening and drawer opening: 20 trials per task, with 90.8%/80.8% success respectively. Each hand–task pair has independent training, action labels, normalization and weights; a new hand requires adaptation and retraining, not a shared cross-hand policy or demonstrated zero-shot transfer to unseen hands. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13119v1) · [Project](https://human2dex.pages.dev/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.3] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-3"></a> | **GNR｜Generative retargeting · Flow matching · Test-time sampling scaling**<br>[Generative Neural Retargeting for Human-to-Robot Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.12440v1)<br>Dechen Gao, Yue Yang, Ben Abbatematteo, Nathan Godwin, Pengcheng Wang, Roger Boldu, Steven Man, Zhiyang Dou, Chuan Qin, Sho Nakagome, Eric Whitmire<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-demonstrations` `generative-retargeting` `physics-based-retargeting` `motion-retargeting` `flow-matching` `residual-control-generation` `mpc-seed-supervision` `mpc-warm-start` `test-time-scaling` `simulation-filtering` `real-to-sim` `demonstration-synthesis` `contact-force-labels` `behavior-cloning` `simulation` | GNR trains a conditional flow-matching model on successful MPC retargeting trajectories to learn residual corrections to IK reference controls, then generates candidates for new human demonstrations and filters them in simulation or refines them with MPC, scaling feasible dexterous demonstration generation at lower sampling cost.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Human hand motion, object poses and meshes are transferred to simulation and IK references. DIAL-MPC provides successful seed controls; the model conditions on reference motion and object geometry/pose to generate residuals added to IK controls. Multiple samples undergo simulated replay, or initialize MPC; pass@S means at least one of S candidates passes, not single-rollout online policy success. Main experiments use SuperDex and Tesollo DG-5F, with Franka FR3 for ShapeFilter/NIST. HOT3D generation yields about 223k trajectories over 3.3k geometries with simulated contact-force labels, plus about 3.4k trajectories for two precise long-horizon tasks. On NIST, pure GNR achieves 4.7% at S=256; GNR-initialized MPC reaches 92.2% with 2,296 samples, showing the need for refinement on difficult tasks. Downstream behavior cloning is validated only in simulation; sim-to-real remains future work. Counts describe generated data; code, full-dataset and weight release status is unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.12440v1) · [Project](https://yy-gx.github.io/GNR/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |

| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.V2R.2] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-v2r-2"></a> | **DexAgent｜Agent-built simulation · Video demonstrations · Data augmentation**<br>[DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.35318v2)<br>Youhui Wang et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-video` `video-to-robot` `human2sim2robot` `agentic-data-generation` `simulation-verification` `trajectory-optimization` `tool-library` `data-augmentation` [vla-fine-tuning](../../../topics/vla.md) `sim-to-real` `bimanual` | **Human2Sim2Robot:** One human demonstration video + task instruction → decompose subtasks and identify object properties → reconstruct a simulation scene → obtain a successful robot trajectory through optimization or code generation with simulation verification → vary initial object/robot states to augment demonstrations and process rendered appearance → fine-tune π₀.₅ on the generated data → deploy on real dexterous hands.<br>**Distinction:** An agent selects or writes tools at each stage and revises outputs using verifier failure feedback. New tools and verifiers persist for later videos; self-evolution means accumulating reusable code, with verification acting during data generation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Bimanual YamBox with two Sharpa hands; 11 tasks. Each task uses one human video and 500 augmented robot demonstrations to fine-tune π₀.₅, evaluated over 10 closed-loop trials with randomized initial object states: 63.6% mean success versus 18.2% for SPIDER, the strongest baseline. Separate open-loop replay passes 11/11 tasks, meaning at least one success in ten trials per task, not perfect trial success. Tasks include rigid, articulated, rope and long-horizon interactions; simulation checks do not eliminate sim-to-real or force-sensitive failures. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.35318v2) · [Project](https://dexagent1.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-23 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.V2R.3] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-v2r-3"></a> | **EgoMatrix｜Contact-consistent reconstruction · RL manipulation transfer · Paired action–video generation**<br>[EgoMatrix: Physically Faithful Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Egocentric Human Videos](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.18822v1)<br>Ziheng Wang, Yanming Shao, Ting Mao, Kaihan Chen, Yiqun Wang, Xuanye Wu, Yao Mu<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `egocentric-video` `human-video` `video-to-robot` `contact-aware-reconstruction` `retargeting` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `reference-tracking` `demonstration-synthesis` `paired-observation-action-data` `joint-hand-object-rendering` `background-transfer` `data-augmentation` `open-loop-replay` | EgoMatrix reconstructs and refines hand–object contact from egocentric human videos, obtains executable bimanual trajectories through retargeting and PPO, then jointly renders robot hands and objects and transfers compatible backgrounds to generate robot demonstrations with synchronized actions and visual observations.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Multi-start pose and local contact refinement reduce contact gaps and penetration. The hands are retargeted independently before a joint bimanual tracking policy is trained with PPO in Isaac Lab using ManipTrans without its pretrained imitator; successful rollouts yield synchronized states, controls and rendered observations. Background transfer applies one rigid transform to the entire interaction, preserving relative motion/contact in task-compatible scenes. Simulation trajectory transfer succeeds for 34/62 demonstrations (54.84%) from TACO, OakInk2 and self-collected videos. Hardware validation replays trajectories on dual UR5e arms with XHand hands. Benefits of synthesized visual observations for downstream manipulation-policy training remain untested. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.18822v1) · [Project](https://spikew726.github.io/EgoMatrix/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.V2R.4] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-v2r-4"></a> | **EgoCPT｜Human-video transfer · Joint contact–force optimization · Residual RL**<br>[EgoCPT: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Ego-Centric Video with Contact-Aware Optimization](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17572v1)<br>Zhixin Sun, Kairui Shi, Tianao Ren, Ming Yang, Mark Cutkosky, James Jingxi Xu<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `human-video` `egocentric-video` `video-to-robot` `physics-aware-retargeting` `contact-aware-optimization` `contact-sampling` `force-allocation` `object-motion-tracking` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `reference-conditioned-policy` `trajectory-generation` `simulation` `open-loop-replay` | EgoCPT recovers object motion from a single egocentric video and reference hand trajectories, searches robot-feasible bimanual interactions through contact sampling, hand-pose optimization and force allocation, then uses PPO residual control to refine execution and generate manipulation trajectories for real-robot replay.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Inputs are RGB video and metric 3D reference hand trajectories. Object motion is fixed while human motion guides robot contact/force search under joint, collision, friction and actuator limits. In simulation, PPO outputs 56 bimanual residuals (6 wrist translations + 6 rotations + 44 finger joints) added to reference motions; optimized forces guide feasibility checks and rewards rather than direct policy torque commands. Sharpa-hand evaluations cover five task families: 52 EgoDex and 25 TACO sequences achieve 67.3% and 92.0% simulated trajectory-tracking success. Hardware demonstrates bimanual trajectory replay, not online closed-loop policy deployment. The method assumes rigid objects; EgoDex inputs with incorrect reconstructed object poses are excluded. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17572v1) · [Project](https://ego-cpt.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.V2R.5] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-v2r-5"></a> | **Hand2Robot｜Human-video transfer · Object-centric 4D reconstruction · VLA post-training**<br>[Hand2Robot: Object-Centric 4D Hand Reconstruction from Human Demonstrations for Robotics](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.15769v1)<br>Zetao Du, Weiqing Wang, Hanbing Zhang, Yimiao Zhou, Ye Shi, Liang Wang, Jingya Wang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-video` `rgb-d` `video-to-robot` `demonstration-synthesis` `object-centric-reconstruction` `hand-object-reconstruction` `confidence-aware-object-tracking` `viterbi-trajectory-selection` `contact-consistent-refinement` `motion-retargeting` `geort` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) [vla-fine-tuning](../../../topics/vla.md) `human-robot-co-training` `real-world` | Hand2Robot selects globally consistent object-pose trajectories from human RGB-D videos, refines hand motion against object references through image alignment, contact and temporal consistency, retargets it into robot action labels, and mixes these with limited robot demonstrations to post-train π₀.₅ for target-task manipulation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Inputs are RGB-D videos and camera intrinsics. VLM parsing precedes Viterbi selection of object trajectories using pose confidence, mask agreement and temporal costs. With objects fixed, staged image/contact refinement and penetration penalties improve hand motion before GeoRT and coordinate alignment produce action labels. Reconstruction is evaluated on DexYCB/HO3D-v3. Franka + xHand tests cover Place Vase, Open Box and Insert Toast. Per task, 20 robot + 100 human demonstrations are sampled 1:1 for training and evaluated in 20 trials; mean success rises from 48.3% with 20 robot demonstrations alone to 80.0%, versus 8.3% with human data alone. Human/robot recordings share a fixed side view; test positions follow the training distribution. Evidence supports target-task post-training, not robot-data-free learning or cross-view generalization. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.15769v1) · [Project](https://hand2robot.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.4] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-4"></a> | **GenDexHand｜Agent-driven generative simulation · VLM scene refinement · Planning + RL**<br>[GenDexHand: Generative Simulation for Dexterous Hands](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.01791v1)<br>Feng Chen, Zhuxiu Xu, Tianzhe Chu, Xunzhe Zhou, Li Sun, Zewen Wu, Shenghua Gao, Zhongyu Li, Yanchao Yang, Yi Ma<br>**Tags:** `agentic-data-generation` `dexterous` `generative-simulation` `llm-task-generation` `vlm-scene-refinement` `subtask-decomposition` `controller-selection` `dof-constraints` `motion-planning` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `reward-code-generation` `successful-trajectory-collection` `simulation` | GenDexHand uses an LLM agent to orchestrate task and simulation-scene generation, a VLM to verify and refine scenes, and subtask decomposition, planner/PPO selection and active-joint constraints to collect successful manipulation trajectories.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Claude Sonnet 4.0 generates tasks/configurations from robot/object assets; Gemini 2.5 Pro checks three-view renders and issues scale/translation/rotation edits applied to scene configurations. This visual loop refines environment generation. An agent assigns planners or RL and active joints per subtask: planners handle reaching/transport; PPO MLP subpolicies (hidden widths 1024/1024/512) learn contact operations from generated reward, evaluation and extra-observation code, with irrelevant DoFs frozen. Outputs are successful trajectories and task environments, rather than one shared multitask policy. SAPIEN experiments use UR10e + ShadowHand, 1,024 parallel environments and 20-Hz control. Quantitative policy comparisons focus on cabinet opening, bottle pickup and apple-to-bowl placement, measuring steps to collect 1,000 successful trajectories; scene showcases do not establish broad policy evaluation. Hardware policy transfer is not demonstrated; cross-hand adaptation needs human expertise, and appendix code-refinement prompts include human feedback. The official repository contains only a README marking code as forthcoming; full generated-data and policy-weight availability is unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.01791v1) · [Project](https://winniechen2002.github.io/GenDexHand/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.5] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-5"></a> | **HumanoidGen｜Agent constraint planning · MCTS plan repair · Bimanual demonstration generation**<br>[HumanoidGen: Data Generation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation via LLM Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.00833v2)<br>Zhi Jing, Siyuan Yang, Jicong Ao, Ting Xiao, Yu-Gang Jiang, Chenjia Bai<br>**Tags:** `agentic-data-generation` `dexterous` `bimanual` `llm-planning` `code-generation` `spatial-point-axis-annotations` `relational-action-constraints` `hand-atomic-operations` `constrained-motion-planning` `trajectory-optimization` `mcts` `simulation-feedback` `successful-prefix-reuse` `scene-augmentation` `diffusion-policy` `imitation-learning` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | HumanoidGen uses an LLM agent to generate bimanual hand-primitive and spatial-constraint programs from hand/object point-axis annotations, uses simulation feedback and MCTS to retain successful prefixes and repair failed plans, and executes constraint-solved motions to collect demonstrations for diffusion-policy training.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Task, scene and hand/object point-axis annotations become bilateral steps, hand primitives and goal/path constraints. SNOPT solves terminal joint configurations, mplib plans constrained paths, and fingers execute predefined primitives. MCTS/STCR segments code, truncates at failures, combines successful operations and stores code/error/scene state to resume search; feedback updates plans/search statistics, not an RL action policy. Collected data trains RGB/proprioceptive DP or point-cloud DP3 using three past observations and eight-step action predictions. HGen-Bench contains 20 tabletop tasks on H1-2 with two Inspire hands: seven DoFs per arm and six per hand, giving 26-D actions, six RGB-D views and over 120 augmented scenes. One hand type is primarily validated; shared-weight cross-hand deployment is not shown. Asset annotations and hand primitives need preparation, with annotation transfer available for similar assets. Two v2 hardware tasks, dual-bottle pickup and laptop closing, each collect 25 real trajectories; DP with 100 simulated plus five real trajectories achieves 13/20 and 14/20, rather than simulation-only zero-shot deployment. Official generation/evaluation code, simulation assets/data and task-specific DP/DP3 models are public; model resources are linked but not locally reproduced. | NeurIPS 2025 / arXiv v2 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.00833v2) · [Project](https://openhumanoidgen.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/TeleHuman/HumanoidGen) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TeleEmbodied/humanoidgen_dataset) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/TeleEmbodied/humanoidgen_model) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
